text:
Nikita Kucherov has asked out of Tampa Bay, and he is playing like a man who wants every front office watching. He scored three goals in Wednesday's 8-3 win in Buffalo, a night that also brought John Carlson's 800th career point and Sam O'Reilly's first. The rumor mill has the Wild, the Mammoth and Montreal circling, and Andrei Vasilevskiy told TSN he hopes "that something will change" between his longtime teammate and the club. However this ends, the Lightning are 4-1-0 in their last five and have outscored teams 23-13.

There are two reasons to temper that tonight. Tampa is on the second night of a back-to-back, and Dennis Hildeby starts over Vasilevskiy, who has 14 of their 18 starts. Hildeby was 10.1 goals saved above expected in 20 games last season, but is at .880 in four this year. And Brayden Point is on injured reserve until early December; Brandon Hagel has moved up beside Jake Guentzel and Kucherov, and O'Reilly gets a look on the top power play. Guentzel plays his 700th NHL game.

Columbus has the harder season to look at. The Blue Jackets have 14 points in 16 games, 49% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of the chances), and an 11.9% chance at the playoffs in our race. Jet Greaves, who saved 15.0 goals above expected last season, is at .879 this year, and The Columbus Dispatch has written about his growing pains. Zach Werenski keeps producing, and Ivan Provorov's return lifted them in a 7-2 win over Colorado last week, but Tuesday's 4-1 loss to Florida was a step back. Matthew Knies has no goals in 15 games on 2.7 expected goals, a drought that is more bad luck than bad play.

Our Sleeper is Tampa fourth-liner Conor Geekie, with 2.0 expected goals in his last ten games in about 11 minutes a night; we give him a 12% chance to score. Mathieu Olivier is one goal from 50 for his career. Our numbers have the Lightning at 3.30 expected goals to Columbus's 2.96.
headline: Kucherov keeps scoring through the trade noise
